-- =============================================================================

-- =============================================================================
-- BEGIN FILE: src/server/Projectile/Spec.luau
-- =============================================================================
--!strict
--!optimize 2
--[[
	Projectile/Spec.luau
	Compiled configs for EFFICIENT projectiles (see Store.luau): everything a
	projectile's normalized config makes constant -- damage, visuals, motion
	constants, bounce/pierce allowances, its raycast filter... -- in one
	frozen table shared by every projectile fired with an equal config, plus
	the handle metatable that reads from it.

	Configs are usually fresh tables per shot, so specs are found by VALUE: a
	trie over the normalized settings (tables by content: IgnoreInstances via
	the shared RaycastParams it produced, Visual by its shallow contents).
	Past MAX_SPECS distinct specs the trie is reset -- live projectiles keep
	theirs, new shots just build new ones.
]]

local Store = require(script.Parent.Store)

local Spec = {}

local MAX_SPECS = 512

local NIL = newproxy() -- (trie key for nil)
local trie: { [any]: any } = {}
local count = 0

-- A shallow table as a key: its sorted contents (nested tables count by
-- identity, so they just don't share).
local function contentKey(value: { [any]: any }): string
	local parts = {}
	for k, v in value do
		table.insert(parts, `{tostring(k)}={typeof(v)}:{tostring(v)}`)
	end
	table.sort(parts)
	return table.concat(parts, "|")
end

-- The spec and handle metatable for these normalized settings (Config.normalize)
-- and movement RaycastParams. `class` is the Projectile class; `lazy` its
-- per-projectile values made on first read (see Store.HandleMetatable).
function Spec.Get(settings: any, rayParams: RaycastParams, class: any, lazy: { [string]: () -> any }): (any, any)
	local visual = settings.Visual
	local keys = {
		settings.Speed, settings.Acceleration, settings.AccelerationDirection, settings.MinSpeed, settings.MaxSpeed,
		settings.Gravity, settings.Radius, settings.Lifetime, settings.MaxRealLifetime, settings.Damage,
		settings.Source, settings.Filter, settings.Bounces, settings.Restitution, settings.Penetration,
		settings.MaxPierces, settings.PierceFalloff, settings.Visualize, settings.VisualRange, settings.Model,
		if visual then contentKey(visual) else nil, settings.VisualScale, settings.DestroyDelay,
		settings.WaitForParticles, settings.WaitForTrails, settings.ActivateParticlesOnCreate, settings.OnBounce,
		rayParams,
	}
	local node = trie
	for index = 1, 28 do
		local key = keys[index]
		if key == nil then
			key = NIL
		end
		local nextNode = node[key]
		if not nextNode then
			nextNode = {}
			node[key] = nextNode
		end
		node = nextNode
	end
	local found = node[NIL]
	if found then
		return found[1], found[2]
	end

	local spec = table.freeze({
		Speed = settings.Speed,
		Acceleration = settings.Acceleration,
		AccelerationDirection = settings.AccelerationDirection,
		MinSpeed = settings.MinSpeed,
		MaxSpeed = settings.MaxSpeed,
		Gravity = settings.Gravity,
		Radius = settings.Radius,
		Lifetime = settings.Lifetime,
		MaxRealLifetime = settings.MaxRealLifetime,
		Damage = settings.Damage,
		DamageMultiplier = 1,
		Source = settings.Source,
		IgnoreInstances = settings.IgnoreInstances,
		Filter = settings.Filter,
		BouncesLeft = settings.Bounces,
		Restitution = settings.Restitution,
		Penetration = settings.Penetration,
		PiercesLeft = settings.MaxPierces,
		PierceFalloff = settings.PierceFalloff,
		HomingDelay = 0,
		ReacquireTimer = 0,
		Visualize = settings.Visualize,
		VisualRange = settings.VisualRange,
		Model = settings.Model,
		Visual = settings.Visual,
		VisualScale = settings.VisualScale,
		DestroyDelay = settings.DestroyDelay,
		WaitForParticles = settings.WaitForParticles,
		WaitForTrails = settings.WaitForTrails,
		ActivateParticlesOnCreate = settings.ActivateParticlesOnCreate,
		OnBounce = settings.OnBounce,
		RewindSeconds = 0,
		_acquireTimer = 0,
		_rewindTime = 0,
		_rayParams = rayParams,
	})
	local metatable = Store.HandleMetatable(spec, class, lazy)
	count += 1
	if count > MAX_SPECS then
		table.clear(trie)
		count = 0
	else
		node[NIL] = { spec, metatable }
	end
	return spec, metatable
end

-- Distinct specs currently cached (Stats).
function Spec.Count(): number
	return count
end

return Spec
-- =============================================================================
-- END FILE: src/server/Projectile/Spec.luau
-- =============================================================================

-- =============================================================================
-- BEGIN FILE: src/server/Projectile/Sweep.luau
-- =============================================================================
--!strict
--!native
--!optimize 2
--[[
	Projectile/Sweep.luau
	The parallel half of projectile movement: the substep loop of
	Projectile.Step for a projectile with no homing and no lag compensation,
	run inside an Actor worker (ProjectileWorkerBootstrap) on a packed copy of
	its state. It plans, casts and integrates exactly as Step does -- same
	ProjectileMotion / ProjectileStepPlanner calls, same constants -- and stops
	at the first contact, handing that substep (and everything after it) back
	to the serial Step code, which owns hits, damage and signals. So a frame
	with no contact is computed entirely here; one with a contact ends in the
	same state it would have without the split.

	Also defines the packed layouts both sides use:
	  input  (48 bytes): motion spec id u32, filter id u32, position 3 x f32,
	         velocity 3 x f32 (Vector3s are float32: exact), age f64,
	         remaining f64. The per-shot constants (acceleration and its
	         direction, gravity, min/max speed, radius, lifetime) are a
	         MotionSpec the workers are sent once and keep, like filters.
	  output (OUTPUT_BYTES): status u8, guard u8, position 3 x f32, velocity
	         3 x f32 (both are Vector3s, float32 already: exact), age f64,
	         remaining f64
]]

local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local Shared = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Shared")
local ProjectileMotion = require(Shared:WaitForChild("Projectile"):WaitForChild("Motion"))
local Math = require(script.Parent.Math)
local Planner = require(Shared:WaitForChild("Projectile"):WaitForChild("StepPlanner"))

local Sweep = {}

Sweep.MaxSubsteps = 16
Sweep.Done = 0 -- loop finished; `remaining` is the carried simulation debt
Sweep.Contact = 1 -- the next substep hits something: resume serially from here
Sweep.Expired = 2 -- lifetime ran out (Step returns false)

local MIN_STEP_DT = ProjectileMotion.MinStepDt
local MAX_SUBSTEPS = Sweep.MaxSubsteps
local DONE, CONTACT, EXPIRED = Sweep.Done, Sweep.Contact, Sweep.Expired

local IN, OUT = 48, 44

-- Byte strides and offsets Parallel's persistent slots update in place.
Sweep.InputStride, Sweep.OutputStride = IN, OUT
Sweep.InputMotion = 8 -- position then velocity, 6 x f32 (same layout as the output's)
Sweep.InputAge = 32
Sweep.InputRemaining = 40
-- output offsets
Sweep.OutStatus, Sweep.OutGuard, Sweep.OutPosition, Sweep.OutVelocity, Sweep.OutAge, Sweep.OutRemaining =
	0, 1, 4, 16, 28, 36

-- A projectile's per-shot motion constants, as the workers keep them (plus
-- its homing constants, when it homes).
export type MotionSpec = {
	Acceleration: number | Vector3,
	Direction: Vector3?,
	Gravity: number | Vector3,
	MinSpeed: number,
	MaxSpeed: number,
	Radius: number,
	Lifetime: number,
	TurnRate: number?, -- rad/s; nil: no homing
	AutoAcquire: boolean?, -- searches for targets itself (AcquireRadius / TargetTag(s))
	Retarget: boolean?, -- re-checks for the nearest target (Retarget and not Permalock)
	-- target searches on the worker (WorkerSearch: no custom Filter): the
	-- frame's target list is matched by TagMask (0: any entity) within
	-- AcquireRadius (nil: unbounded); timers reset like Homing.update's
	WorkerSearch: boolean?,
	TagMask: number?,
	AcquireRadius: number?,
	AcquireInterval: number?,
	ReacquireRate: number?,
}

-- This frame's homing targets for the workers (Parallel.Dispatch): every
-- eligible entity's position and tag bits.
export type HomingFrame = { Positions: { Vector3 }, Bits: { number } }

-- Homing steers at most this many radians per substep (Projectile.Step uses
-- the same cap, so worker and serial substeps match).
Sweep.MaxHomingTurnStep = math.rad(5)

-- Per-frame homing state, in a separate buffer per batch (only homing items
-- use it): flags u8 (HOMING, TARGET_POSITION: the target exists and has a
-- position, HAS_TARGET: HomingTarget is set, EXPLICIT: it's the config's own
-- Target), the index of its own Source in the frame's target list u32 at 4
-- (0: none; never picked), target position 3 x f32 at 8, HomingDelay f64 at
-- 24, _acquireTimer f64 at 32, ReacquireTimer f64 at 40. The worker hands back
-- the three timers and a target change f64 (0: unchanged, -1: none found, >0:
-- the frame target list index it picked) -- 32 bytes per item.
Sweep.HomingInStride, Sweep.HomingOutStride = 48, 32
Sweep.HomingFlag, Sweep.HomingTargetPosition, Sweep.HomingHasTarget, Sweep.HomingExplicit = 1, 2, 4, 8
local HOMING_IN, HOMING_OUT = 48, 32

-- The nearest of the frame's targets matching `mask` within `radius` of
-- `position`, skipping `exclude` (Homing.acquireTarget's rule, distance <=
-- best). 0 if none.
local function searchTarget(frame: HomingFrame, position: Vector3, radius: number?, mask: number, exclude: number): number
	local best, bestDistance = 0, radius or math.huge
	local positions, bits = frame.Positions, frame.Bits
	for index = 1, #positions do
		if index ~= exclude and (mask == 0 or bit32.band(bits[index], mask) ~= 0) then
			local distance = (positions[index] - position).Magnitude
			if distance <= bestDistance then
				best, bestDistance = index, distance
			end
		end
	end
	return best
end

-- A homing item's timers where its frame ended (or was handed back), and
-- its target change.
local function writeTimers(homingOut: buffer?, item: number, d: number, a: number, r: number, change: number)
	if homingOut then
		local h = (item - 1) * HOMING_OUT
		buffer.writef64(homingOut, h, d)
		buffer.writef64(homingOut, h + 8, a)
		buffer.writef64(homingOut, h + 16, r)
		buffer.writef64(homingOut, h + 24, change)
	end
end

local writef64, readf64 = buffer.writef64, buffer.readf64
local writef32, readf32, writeu8, readu8 = buffer.writef32, buffer.readf32, buffer.writeu8, buffer.readu8
local writeu32, readu32 = buffer.writeu32, buffer.readu32

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Packing
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

function Sweep.InputSize(count: number): number
	return count * IN
end

function Sweep.OutputSize(count: number): number
	return count * OUT
end

local function writeVector32(b: buffer, offset: number, v: Vector3)
	writef32(b, offset, v.X)
	writef32(b, offset + 4, v.Y)
	writef32(b, offset + 8, v.Z)
end

local function readVector32(b: buffer, offset: number): Vector3
	return Vector3.new(readf32(b, offset), readf32(b, offset + 4), readf32(b, offset + 8))
end

-- The motion spec of `p` (its per-shot constants; see MotionSpec).
function Sweep.SpecOf(p: any): MotionSpec
	local homing = p.Homing
	return {
		Acceleration = p.Acceleration or 0,
		Direction = p.AccelerationDirection,
		Gravity = p.Gravity or 0,
		MinSpeed = p.MinSpeed,
		MaxSpeed = p.MaxSpeed,
		Radius = p.Radius,
		Lifetime = p.Lifetime,
		TurnRate = homing and homing.TurnRate,
		AutoAcquire = homing and (homing.AcquireRadius ~= nil or homing.TargetTag ~= nil or homing.TargetTags ~= nil),
		Retarget = homing and (homing.Retarget and not homing.Permalock),
		WorkerSearch = homing and p.Filter == nil,
		AcquireRadius = homing and homing.AcquireRadius,
		AcquireInterval = homing and homing.AcquireInterval,
		ReacquireRate = homing and homing.ReacquireRate,
		-- (TagMask is filled in by Parallel, which owns the tag bits)
	}
end

-- WriteInput from plain values (a freshly fired projectile; Parallel.PackNew).
function Sweep.WriteInputValues(b: buffer, item: number, spec: number, filter: number, position: Vector3,
	velocity: Vector3, age: number, remaining: number)
	local o = (item - 1) * IN
	writeu32(b, o, spec)
	writeu32(b, o + 4, filter)
	writeVector32(b, o + 8, position)
	writeVector32(b, o + 20, velocity)
	writef64(b, o + 32, age)
	writef64(b, o + 40, remaining)
end

function Sweep.WriteInput(b: buffer, item: number, spec: number, filter: number, p: any, remaining: number)
	local o = (item - 1) * IN
	writeu32(b, o, spec)
	writeu32(b, o + 4, filter)
	writeVector32(b, o + 8, p.Position)
	writeVector32(b, o + 20, p.Velocity)
	writef64(b, o + 32, p.Age)
	writef64(b, o + 40, remaining)
end

function Sweep.WriteOutput(b: buffer, item: number, status: number, position: Vector3, velocity: Vector3, age: number, remaining: number, guard: number)
	local o = (item - 1) * OUT
	writeu8(b, o, status)
	writeu8(b, o + 1, guard)
	writeVector32(b, o + 4, position)
	writeVector32(b, o + 16, velocity)
	writef64(b, o + 28, age)
	writef64(b, o + 36, remaining)
end

-- One result as plain values (no table): status, position, velocity, age,
-- remaining, guard.
function Sweep.ReadOutputValues(b: buffer, item: number): (number, Vector3, Vector3, number, number, number)
	local o = (item - 1) * OUT
	return readu8(b, o), readVector32(b, o + 4), readVector32(b, o + 16), readf64(b, o + 28),
		readf64(b, o + 36), readu8(b, o + 1)
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The loop
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Runs one packed projectile and writes its result. `specs` are the motion
-- specs this worker has been sent; `castHits(from, displacement, radius,
-- filter)` is the worker's movement cast (occupancy skip +
-- Raycast/Spherecast); `hasEntities(position)` its mirror of
-- Raycast.chunkHasEntities.
function Sweep.Run(
	input: buffer,
	item: number,
	output: buffer,
	uniformTime: boolean,
	specs: { [number]: MotionSpec },
	castHits: (Vector3, Vector3, number, number, boolean) -> any,
	hasEntities: (Vector3) -> boolean,
	onContact: ((item: number, from: Vector3, displacement: Vector3, hit: any) -> ())?,
	homingIn: buffer?,
	homingOut: buffer?,
	homingFrame: HomingFrame?
)
	local o = (item - 1) * IN
	local filter = readu32(input, o + 4)
	local position = readVector32(input, o + 8)
	local velocity = readVector32(input, o + 20)
	local age = readf64(input, o + 32)
	local remaining = readf64(input, o + 40)
	local spec = specs[readu32(input, o)]
	if not spec then
		-- unknown spec: hand the whole frame to the serial path
		Sweep.WriteOutput(output, item, CONTACT, position, velocity, age, remaining, 0)
		return
	end
	local acceleration, direction, gravity = spec.Acceleration, spec.Direction, spec.Gravity
	local minSpeed, maxSpeed, radius, lifetime = spec.MinSpeed, spec.MaxSpeed, spec.Radius, spec.Lifetime

	-- Homing (Homing.update, per substep): steering toward the target's
	-- position this frame. A target search due mid-frame is made here, from
	-- the frame's target list (WorkerSearch); a config with a custom Filter
	-- hands the substep back for the main thread to search instead.
	local turnRate = spec.TurnRate
	local homingFlags = 0
	local targetPosition = Vector3.zero
	local delay, acquireTimer, reacquireTimer = 0, 0, 0
	local exclude = 0
	if homingIn and turnRate then
		local h = (item - 1) * HOMING_IN
		homingFlags = readu8(homingIn, h)
		if homingFlags ~= 0 then
			exclude = readu32(homingIn, h + 4)
			targetPosition = readVector32(homingIn, h + 8)
			delay, acquireTimer, reacquireTimer = readf64(homingIn, h + 24), readf64(homingIn, h + 32), readf64(homingIn, h + 40)
		end
	end
	local homing = homingFlags ~= 0
	local hasTargetPosition = bit32.btest(homingFlags, 2)
	local hasTarget = bit32.btest(homingFlags, 4)
	local explicit = bit32.btest(homingFlags, 8)
	local targetChange = 0
	local workerSearch = homing and spec.WorkerSearch == true and homingFrame ~= nil

	-- Mirrors Projectile.Step's loop (no rewind: no lag-compensated entity
	-- check).
	local guard = 0
	while remaining > MIN_STEP_DT and guard < MAX_SUBSTEPS do
		guard += 1
		local lifeRemaining = lifetime - age
		if lifeRemaining <= MIN_STEP_DT then
			if homing then writeTimers(homingOut, item, delay, acquireTimer, reacquireTimer, targetChange) end
			Sweep.WriteOutput(output, item, EXPIRED, position, velocity, age, remaining, guard)
			return
		end

		local accelerationVector = ProjectileMotion.GetAcceleration(velocity, acceleration, direction, gravity)
		local sample, chunkScale = Planner.Sample(position, velocity, accelerationVector, uniformTime)
		if chunkScale <= 0 then
			remaining = 0
			break
		end
		local highRes = hasEntities(sample)
		local maxDt = if homing and hasTarget and (turnRate :: number) > 0
			then Sweep.MaxHomingTurnStep / (turnRate :: number)
			else math.huge
		local stepDt = Planner.StepDt(position, velocity, accelerationVector, chunkScale, remaining, lifeRemaining,
			highRes, uniformTime, maxDt)
		if stepDt <= 0 then
			break
		end

		-- (what this substep starts from, for handing it back untouched)
		local startVelocity, startDelay, startAcquire, startReacquire = velocity, delay, acquireTimer, reacquireTimer
		if homing then
			if delay > 0 then
				delay -= stepDt
			else
				local searchDue = false
				if not hasTargetPosition then
					if spec.AutoAcquire then
						if acquireTimer - stepDt <= 0 then
							searchDue = true
						else
							acquireTimer -= stepDt
						end
					end
				elseif spec.Retarget and not explicit then
					if reacquireTimer - stepDt <= 0 then
						searchDue = true
					else
						reacquireTimer -= stepDt
					end
				end
				if searchDue then
					if not workerSearch then
						-- the main thread searches (a custom Filter): hand this substep back
						writeTimers(homingOut, item, startDelay, startAcquire, startReacquire, targetChange)
						Sweep.WriteOutput(output, item, CONTACT, position, startVelocity, age, remaining, guard - 1)
						return
					end
					-- (as Homing.update: reset the timer, then search from here)
					if hasTargetPosition then
						reacquireTimer = spec.ReacquireRate :: number
					else
						acquireTimer = (spec.AcquireInterval :: number) * (0.5 + math.random())
					end
					local found = searchTarget(homingFrame :: HomingFrame, position, spec.AcquireRadius, spec.TagMask or 0, exclude)
					if found > 0 then
						targetChange = found
						targetPosition = (homingFrame :: HomingFrame).Positions[found]
						hasTargetPosition, hasTarget, explicit = true, true, false
					else
						targetChange = -1
						hasTargetPosition, hasTarget, explicit = false, false, false
					end
				end
				if hasTargetPosition then
					local speed = velocity.Magnitude
					velocity = Math.rotateTowards(velocity, targetPosition - position, (turnRate :: number) * stepDt) * speed
				end
			end
		end

		local endVelocity, movementVelocity = ProjectileMotion.Integrate(velocity, acceleration, direction, gravity,
			minSpeed, maxSpeed, stepDt)
		local displacement = movementVelocity * stepDt
		local hit = castHits(position, displacement, radius, filter, highRes)
		if hit then
			-- hand this substep back untouched; Step redoes it serially (with
			-- this cast's result, so it needn't cast it again -- see onContact)
			if onContact and hit ~= true then
				onContact(item, position, displacement, hit)
			end
			writeTimers(homingOut, item, startDelay, startAcquire, startReacquire, targetChange)
			Sweep.WriteOutput(output, item, CONTACT, position, startVelocity, age, remaining, guard - 1)
			return
		end
		velocity = endVelocity
		position += displacement
		age += stepDt
		remaining -= stepDt / chunkScale
		if age >= lifetime - MIN_STEP_DT then
			if homing then writeTimers(homingOut, item, delay, acquireTimer, reacquireTimer, targetChange) end
			Sweep.WriteOutput(output, item, EXPIRED, position, velocity, age, remaining, guard)
			return
		end
	end
	if homing then writeTimers(homingOut, item, delay, acquireTimer, reacquireTimer, targetChange) end
	Sweep.WriteOutput(output, item, DONE, position, velocity, age, remaining, guard)
end

return Sweep
-- =============================================================================
-- END FILE: src/server/Projectile/Sweep.luau
-- =============================================================================

-- =============================================================================
-- BEGIN FILE: src/server/Projectile/Profile.luau
-- =============================================================================
--!strict
--!native
--!optimize 2
--[[
	Projectile/Profile.luau
	Where the main thread's projectile time goes, for the debug panel's Stats
	tab: named sections accumulate seconds, and Take() returns each as average
	ms per frame since the last call.

	Per-projectile parts are SAMPLED (one projectile in SAMPLE is timed and the
	result scaled up) so the timer calls don't distort the very loops being
	measured; those sections are estimates, labelled as such in the Stats tab.
]]

local Profile = {}

Profile.SAMPLE = 32 -- time one projectile in this many in per-projectile loops

local totals: { [string]: number } = {}
local counts: { [string]: number } = {}
local frames = 0

function Profile.Add(name: string, seconds: number)
	totals[name] = (totals[name] or 0) + seconds
end

-- A per-frame count (reported as the average per frame, not ms).
function Profile.Count(name: string, n: number)
	counts[name] = (counts[name] or 0) + n
end

-- Lua heap at the last frame, and how much the garbage collector freed
-- since the last Take (heap drops between frames).
local lastHeap = gcinfo()
local freedKB = 0

-- One server frame passed (called once per projectile Heartbeat step).
function Profile.Frame()
	frames += 1
	local heap = gcinfo()
	if heap < lastHeap then
		freedKB += lastHeap - heap
	end
	lastHeap = heap
end

-- { [section] = average ms per frame, [count] = average per frame } since
-- the last call, then resets.
function Profile.Take(): { [string]: number }
	local result = {}
	local count = math.max(frames, 1)
	for name, seconds in totals do
		result[name] = seconds / count * 1000
	end
	for name, n in counts do
		result[name] = n / count
	end
	result.HeapMB = lastHeap / 1024
	result.GcFreedMB = freedKB / 1024 / count
	freedKB = 0
	table.clear(totals)
	table.clear(counts)
	frames = 0
	return result
end

return Profile
-- =============================================================================
-- END FILE: src/server/Projectile/Profile.luau
-- =============================================================================

-- =============================================================================
-- BEGIN FILE: src/server/Projectile/ApplyPass.luau
-- =============================================================================
--!strict
--!native
--!optimize 2
--[[
	Projectile/ApplyPass.luau
	Pass 1 of Parallel.Apply, on its own: every worker result that is a plain
	"moved, hit nothing" for a projectile nothing touched is written straight
	into Store's columns and its slot's packed record; the rest are listed
	for the serial pass. Kept in a small module of its own so it gets native
	code generation regardless of the rest of Parallel.
]]

local SafeMath = require(game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage"):WaitForChild("Shared"):WaitForChild("SafeMath"))
local Sweep = require(script.Parent.Sweep)
local Store = require(script.Parent.Store)

local IN, OUT = Sweep.InputStride, Sweep.OutputStride
local IN_MOTION, IN_AGE, IN_REMAINING = Sweep.InputMotion, Sweep.InputAge, Sweep.InputRemaining
local OUT_STATUS, OUT_POSITION, OUT_AGE, OUT_REMAINING = Sweep.OutStatus, Sweep.OutPosition, Sweep.OutAge, Sweep.OutRemaining
local S_MOTION, S_TIME, S_MARK, S_SCALE = Store.MotionStride, Store.TimeStride, Store.MarkStride, Store.ScaleStride
local S_HOMING, HOMING_OUT = Store.HomingStride, Sweep.HomingOutStride
local DEAD_OR_DIRTY = bit32.bor(Store.Dead, Store.Dirty)
local SWEEP_DONE = Sweep.Done
local LIMIT = SafeMath.Limit

-- Returns dropped, deferred, kept counts; fills `released` (items whose slot
-- to release) and `deferred` (items for the serial pass).
return function(motion: buffer, times: buffer, marks: buffer, flagsColumn: buffer, scalesColumn: buffer,
	data: buffer, input: buffer, count: number, slots: { number }, generations: { number }, scales: { number },
	deadlines: { number }, generationOf: { number }, sources: { any }, now: number, mark: number,
	released: { number }, deferred: { number }, homing: { boolean }?, homingOut: buffer?,
	homingTimers: buffer): (number, number, number)
	local dropped, slow, kept = 0, 0, 0
	for item = 1, count do
		local slot = slots[item]
		if generationOf[slot] ~= generations[item] then
			-- released since (the step loop dropped it): nothing to apply
			dropped += 1
			released[dropped] = item
			continue
		end
		local out = (item - 1) * OUT
		local plain = buffer.readu8(data, out + OUT_STATUS) == SWEEP_DONE
			and bit32.band(buffer.readu8(flagsColumn, slot), DEAD_OR_DIRTY) == 0 and now < deadlines[item]
		if plain then
			-- its scale is still the one it was sent with (own * source's; anything
			-- unusual goes to the serial code, which uses combinedTimeScale)
			local s = slot * S_SCALE
			local own = buffer.readf64(scalesColumn, s)
			local index = buffer.readu32(scalesColumn, s + 8)
			local sourceScale: any = if index ~= 0 then sources[index].TimeScale else 1
			plain = type(sourceScale) == "number" and sourceScale >= 0 and own >= 0 and sourceScale < LIMIT
				and own < LIMIT and sourceScale * own == scales[item]
		end
		if not plain then
			slow += 1
			deferred[slow] = item
			continue
		end
		-- position/velocity are float32 in the output, the column and the slot
		buffer.copy(motion, slot * S_MOTION, data, out + OUT_POSITION, 24)
		local age = buffer.readf64(data, out + OUT_AGE)
		local debt = buffer.readf64(data, out + OUT_REMAINING)
		local t = slot * S_TIME
		buffer.writef64(times, t, age)
		buffer.writef64(times, t + 8, debt)
		if homing and homing[item] and homingOut then
			-- (a homing item's timers, as the worker left them)
			buffer.copy(homingTimers, slot * S_HOMING, homingOut, (item - 1) * HOMING_OUT, 24)
		end
		local i = (item - 1) * IN
		buffer.copy(input, i + IN_MOTION, data, out + OUT_POSITION, 24)
		buffer.writef64(input, i + IN_AGE, age)
		buffer.writef64(input, i + IN_REMAINING, debt) -- (dispatch adds next frame's budget)
		local px = buffer.readf32(data, out + OUT_POSITION)
		local py = buffer.readf32(data, out + OUT_POSITION + 4)
		local pz = buffer.readf32(data, out + OUT_POSITION + 8)
		if math.abs(px) <= LIMIT and math.abs(py) <= LIMIT and math.abs(pz) <= LIMIT then
			buffer.writei32(marks, slot * S_MARK, mark)
			kept += 1
		else
			-- flew past SafeMath.Limit: dies in the step loop
			buffer.writei32(marks, slot * S_MARK, -mark)
			dropped += 1
			released[dropped] = item
		end
	end
	return dropped, slow, kept
end
-- =============================================================================
-- END FILE: src/server/Projectile/ApplyPass.luau
-- =============================================================================

-- =============================================================================
-- BEGIN FILE: src/server/Projectile/Parallel.luau
-- =============================================================================
--!strict
--!native
--!optimize 2
--[[
	Projectile/Parallel.luau
	Main-thread side of parallel projectile movement.

	Each worker Actor owns a batch of SLOTS. A slot holds one projectile's
	packed movement record (Sweep's input layout) and what the projectile
	looked like after the last frame, and it persists across frames: a
	projectile that just flies is packed once, and from then on its record is
	updated straight from the worker's output. Together with Store.luau (the
	projectile's own hot fields in a buffer), a projectile that just flies
	costs the main thread only buffer reads and writes per frame -- its table
	(at tens of thousands of projectiles, mostly cache misses) isn't touched.

	  Offer()                 a projectile that stepped serially (or was just
	                          made) asks for a slot; it's queued.
	  PreSimulation (serial)  Dispatch(): queued projectiles that are eligible --
	                          no homing, no lag compensation, not frozen,
	                          finite state, raycast filter already known to the
	                          workers -- are packed into the emptiest batch;
	                          then every slot's step budget is written and each
	                          batch is sent off.
	  parallel phase          workers (ProjectileWorkerBootstrap) run Sweep.Run:
	                          plan, cast, integrate, stop at the first contact.
	  Heartbeat (serial)      Apply(): a plain "moved, hit nothing" result for a
	                          projectile nothing touched is written straight
	                          into its Store record and its slot. Anything else
	                          goes to Projectile's applier (the serial code),
	                          which answers Refresh (repack, or release if no
	                          longer eligible) or Drop (dead: release). A late
	                          batch is released whole.

	Anything changed behind a slot's back (an ability moved it, a time scale
	changed...) shows up as the record's Dirty flag or a different scale, and
	the projectile is stepped serially -- so the slot never has to be told.

	Workers mirror what they need: time scales/zones (sent when
	ChunkManager.GetTimeVersion changes), raycast filters (sent once per
	distinct filter, usable from the next frame), and which chunks hold
	entities (with every batch). Occupancy masks are baked once and copied to
	each worker at startup, followed by changed-cell deltas.

	Worker raycasts run in the parallel phase that follows PreSimulation, i.e.
	against the world as it was before this frame's physics step; the serial
	path casts after it. Static geometry is identical; moving parts can differ
	by one physics step.
]]

local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local ServerScriptService = game:GetService("ServerScriptService")

local Shared = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Shared")
local ChunkManager = require(Shared:WaitForChild("ChunkManager"))
local Sweep = require(script.Parent.Sweep)
local Store = require(script.Parent.Store)
local ApplyPass = require(script.Parent.ApplyPass)
local Homing = require(script.Parent.Homing)
local Replication = require(script.Parent.Replication)
local Entity = require(Shared:WaitForChild("Entity"))

-- Homing target tags -> a bit each (a spec's TagMask; 0 means any entity).
local tagBits: { [string]: number } = {}
local tagCount = 0
local function tagMaskOf(homing: any): number
	local tags = homing and (homing.TargetTags or (homing.TargetTag and { homing.TargetTag }))
	if not tags then
		return 0
	end
	local mask = 0
	for _, tag in tags do
		local bitValue = tagBits[tag]
		if not bitValue then
			if tagCount >= 30 then
				return -1 -- (too many distinct tags: never matches on a worker)
			end
			tagCount += 1
			bitValue = bit32.lshift(1, tagCount - 1)
			tagBits[tag] = bitValue
		end
		mask = bit32.bor(mask, bitValue)
	end
	return mask
end

-- This frame's homing targets (built at dispatch while anything homes): the
-- entities, their positions and tag bits for the workers, and entity -> index.
local frameTargets: { any } = {}
local frameTargetIndex: { [any]: number } = {}
local homingFrame: Sweep.HomingFrame = { Positions = {}, Bits = {} }

local function buildHomingFrame()
	table.clear(frameTargets)
	table.clear(frameTargetIndex)
	table.clear(homingFrame.Positions)
	table.clear(homingFrame.Bits)
	for _, entity in Entity.GetAll() do
		if entity.IsDestroyed then
			continue
		end
		local bits = 0
		for tag, bitValue in tagBits do
			if entity:HasTag(tag) then
				bits = bit32.bor(bits, bitValue)
			end
		end
		local index = #frameTargets + 1
		frameTargets[index] = entity
		frameTargetIndex[entity] = index
		homingFrame.Positions[index] = entity:GetPosition()
		homingFrame.Bits[index] = bits
	end
end

-- target -> its position this dispatch (many projectiles can hunt one target)
local goalCache: { [any]: Vector3 | false } = {}
local function goalOf(target: any): Vector3?
	if target == nil then
		return nil
	end
	local cached = goalCache[target]
	if cached == nil then
		cached = Homing.targetPosition(target) or false
		goalCache[target] = cached
	end
	return cached or nil
end
local Profile = require(script.Parent.Profile)
local SafeMath = require(Shared:WaitForChild("SafeMath"))

local Parallel = {}

Parallel.Enabled = true
Parallel.MinProjectiles = 32 -- below this, dispatch overhead isn't worth it

-- What an applier returns for a result (see Parallel.Apply).
Parallel.Drop = 0 -- dead: release the slot
Parallel.Refresh = 2 -- alive, but the serial code finished the frame: repack or release
local REFRESH = Parallel.Refresh

-- projectile._parallelState
local QUEUED, SLOTTED = 1, 2

local IN, OUT = Sweep.InputStride, Sweep.OutputStride
local IN_MOTION = Sweep.InputMotion
local OUT_STATUS, OUT_POSITION, OUT_VELOCITY = Sweep.OutStatus, Sweep.OutPosition, Sweep.OutVelocity
local OUT_AGE, OUT_REMAINING = Sweep.OutAge, Sweep.OutRemaining
local IN_AGE, IN_REMAINING = Sweep.InputAge, Sweep.InputRemaining
local MIN_CAPACITY = 64
local readf64, writef64, readf32, writef32, bufferCopy = buffer.readf64, buffer.writef64, buffer.readf32, buffer.writef32, buffer.copy
local readu8, readu32, writeu8, band = buffer.readu8, buffer.readu32, buffer.writeu8, bit32.band
local S_MOTION, S_TIME, S_MARK, S_SCALE = Store.MotionStride, Store.TimeStride, Store.MarkStride, Store.ScaleStride
local writei32 = buffer.writei32
local DEAD_OR_DIRTY = bit32.bor(Store.Dead, Store.Dirty)
local SWEEP_DONE = Sweep.Done
local LIMIT = SafeMath.Limit
local abs = math.abs

type Worker = { Actor: Actor, Id: number }
-- A worker's latest result, as fired through ProjectileActors.Results.
type Result = { Frame: number, Count: number, Ms: number, Data: buffer?, Checks: number, Skipped: number, Contacts: any,
	HomingOut: buffer? }
local results: { [number]: Result } = {} -- worker id -> latest

-- Receives a result Apply can't take directly and says what happens to its
-- slot (Refresh or Drop): the projectile, the result (status, position,
-- velocity, age, remaining, guard), whether it was changed since it was
-- packed (Dirty), the scale it was sent with, and the dispatch's time version
-- and uniform-time flag.
export type Applier = (projectile: any, status: number, position: Vector3, velocity: Vector3, age: number,
	remaining: number, guard: number, dirty: boolean, fromScale: number, timeVersion: number,
	uniform: boolean, contact: WorkerContact?, homingTimers: { number }?) -> number

-- A worker's contact for a result that stopped at one: the segment it cast
-- and what it hit, so the serial code can resolve it without casting again.
export type WorkerContact = { From: Vector3, Displacement: Vector3, Instance: Instance, Position: Vector3,
	Normal: Vector3, Distance: number }

-- A worker's slots, item 1..Count (compact: released slots are swap-removed).
type Batch = {
	Count: number,
	Sent: number, -- items dispatched this frame (0: nothing to apply)
	Capacity: number,
	Input: buffer,
	Projectiles: { any },
	Slot: { number }, -- its Store record
	Generation: { number }, -- Store.Generation[slot] when packed (a mismatch: released since)
	Scale: { number },
	Deadline: { number }, -- os.clock() past which MaxRealLifetime is up
	Homing: { boolean }, -- the item homes (its state goes in HomingIn each dispatch)
	-- (cached at pack, for dispatch: its Homing table, Source, and whether a
	-- custom Filter keeps its target searches on the main thread)
	HomingConfig: { any },
	HomingSource: { any },
	HomingMainSearch: { boolean },
	HomingCount: number,
	HomingIn: buffer?,
}

local workers: { Worker } = {}
local frame = 0
local sentTimeVersion = -1
local filterIds: { [any]: any } = {} -- instance trie -> { [flags]: id }
local filterReady: { [number]: number } = {} -- id -> first frame workers have it
local nextFilterId = 0
local specIds: { [any]: any } = {} -- trie of motion-spec values -> id
local specReady: { [number]: number } = {} -- id -> first frame workers have it
local nextSpecId = 0
local MAX_SPECS = 65535 -- past this many distinct specs, new ones just step serially
local batches: { Batch } = {}
local batchUniform = true
local batchTimeVersion = 0
local running = false -- the last Dispatch sent batches
local inFlight = false -- between a Dispatch and its Apply
local queue: { any } = {}
local scaleOf: (any) -> number? = function()
	return nil
end
local released: { number } = {} -- scratch for Apply
local deferred: { number } = {} -- scratch for Apply
local homingTimers: { number } = { 0, 0, 0 } -- scratch for Apply

local stats = { Parallel = 0, Resumed = 0, Serial = 0, Fallback = 0, Late = 0, Frames = 0, SlowestWorkerMs = 0, WorkerMs = 0,
	AppliedFrames = 0, WorkerChecks = 0, WorkerSkipped = 0 }
-- workers' reasons a cast wasn't skipped: not ready, too wide, outside terrain, blocked, blocked by a moving part
local workerReasons = { 0, 0, 0, 0, 0 }

-- Rescanned whenever an actor is added or removed (the bootstrap may still be
-- creating them when the first dispatch runs). Returns true when the list
-- changed, so Dispatch can release every slot (batches follow worker order).
local workersStale = true
local actorsRoot: Instance? = nil
local resultsConnected = false

local function refreshWorkers(): boolean
	if not workersStale then
		return false
	end
	local root = actorsRoot or ServerScriptService:FindFirstChild("ProjectileActors", true)
	local event = root and root:FindFirstChild("Results")
	if not root or not event then
		return false
	end
	if not actorsRoot then
		actorsRoot = root
		root.ChildAdded:Connect(function()
			workersStale = true
		end)
		root.ChildRemoved:Connect(function()
			workersStale = true
		end)
	end
	workersStale = false
	table.clear(workers)
	for _, child in root:GetChildren() do
		local id = tonumber(string.match(child.Name, "(%d+)$"))
		if child:IsA("Actor") and id then
			table.insert(workers, { Actor = child, Id = id })
		end
	end
	table.sort(workers, function(x, y)
		return x.Id < y.Id
	end)
	if not resultsConnected then
		resultsConnected = true
		local resultsEvent = event :: BindableEvent
		resultsEvent.Event:Connect(function(id: number, resultFrame: number, count: number, ms: number,
			data: buffer, checks: number, skipped: number, reasons: { number }?, contacts: any, homingOut: buffer?)
			local result = results[id]
			if not result then
				result = { Frame = 0, Count = 0, Ms = 0, Data = nil, Checks = 0, Skipped = 0, Contacts = nil, HomingOut = nil }
				results[id] = result
			end
			result.Frame, result.Count, result.Ms, result.Data = resultFrame, count, ms, data
			result.Contacts = contacts
			result.HomingOut = homingOut
			stats.WorkerChecks += checks
			stats.WorkerSkipped += skipped
			if reasons then
				for index = 1, 5 do
					workerReasons[index] += reasons[index] or 0
				end
				-- (6: that worker's moving-part count; the largest is kept)
				workerReasons[6] = math.max(workerReasons[6] or 0, reasons[6] or 0)
				workerReasons[7] = reasons[7] or workerReasons[7] -- (7: a worker's largest moving part, by name)
				-- (8 / 9: engine Spherecasts / Raycasts the worker made)
				workerReasons[8] = (workerReasons[8] or 0) + (reasons[8] or 0)
				workerReasons[9] = (workerReasons[9] or 0) + (reasons[9] or 0)
			end
		end)
	end
	return true
end

-- Filter id for a projectile's movement RaycastParams, by content (beam
-- samples rebuild identical params per packet). New ids are sent to every
-- worker and become usable next frame.
local filterByParams: { [RaycastParams]: number } = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" }) :: any

local function filterFor(projectile: any): number?
	local params: RaycastParams = projectile._rayParams
	-- params are shared between projectiles (Raycast.buildRayParams), so most
	-- lookups end here, without reading FilterDescendantsInstances back (and
	-- nothing is written to the projectile, which for an efficient one would
	-- mean a per-projectile override table)
	local known = filterByParams[params]
	if known then
		return if filterReady[known] <= frame then known else nil
	end
	local instances = params.FilterDescendantsInstances
	local node = filterIds
	for _, instance in instances do
		local nextNode = node[instance]
		if not nextNode then
			nextNode = {}
			node[instance] = nextNode
		end
		node = nextNode
	end
	local flags = `{params.IgnoreWater}|{params.CollisionGroup}`
	local id = node[flags]
	if not id then
		nextFilterId += 1
		id = nextFilterId
		node[flags] = id
		filterReady[id] = frame + 1
		for _, worker in workers do
			worker.Actor:SendMessage("Filter", id, instances, params.IgnoreWater, params.CollisionGroup)
		end
	end
	filterByParams[params] = id
	return if filterReady[id] <= frame then id else nil
end

local function syncTimeWorld()
	local version = ChunkManager.GetTimeVersion()
	if version == sentTimeVersion then
		return
	end
	sentTimeVersion = version
	local chunks = {}
	for _, chunk in ChunkManager.GetAllChunks() do
		if chunk.TimeScale ~= 1 then
			table.insert(chunks, { Key = chunk.Key, Scale = chunk.TimeScale })
		end
	end
	local zones = {}
	for _, zone in ChunkManager.GetTimeScaleZones() do
		table.insert(zones, { Id = zone.Id, Position = zone.Position, Radius = zone.Radius, Scale = zone.Scale })
	end
	for _, worker in workers do
		worker.Actor:SendMessage("TimeWorld", ChunkManager.ChunkSize, ChunkManager.UseY, chunks, zones)
	end
end

local function entityChunkKeys(): { Vector3 }
	local keys = {}
	for key in ChunkManager.GetEntityChunkMask() do
		table.insert(keys, key)
	end
	return keys
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Slots
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local function newBatch(): Batch
	return {
		Count = 0, Sent = 0, Capacity = MIN_CAPACITY, Input = buffer.create(Sweep.InputSize(MIN_CAPACITY)),
		Projectiles = {}, Slot = {}, Generation = {}, Scale = {}, Deadline = {}, Homing = {}, HomingCount = 0, HomingIn = nil,
		HomingConfig = {}, HomingSource = {}, HomingMainSearch = {},
	}
end

-- Resizes a batch's input buffer, keeping its records.
local function setHoming(batch: Batch, item: number, homes: boolean)
	local was = batch.Homing[item] == true
	if was ~= homes then
		batch.HomingCount += if homes then 1 else -1
	end
	batch.Homing[item] = homes
end

local function resize(batch: Batch, capacity: number)
	local input = buffer.create(Sweep.InputSize(capacity))
	bufferCopy(input, 0, batch.Input, 0, batch.Count * IN)
	batch.Input, batch.Capacity = input, capacity
end

-- Packs `projectile` into slot `item` (new or reused) with its current state.
local function pack(batch: Batch, item: number, projectile: any, filter: number, spec: number, scale: number)
	local slot = projectile._slot
	batch.Projectiles[item] = projectile
	batch.Slot[item] = slot
	batch.Generation[item] = Store.Generation[slot]
	batch.Scale[item] = scale
	batch.Deadline[item] = projectile._spawnRealTime + projectile.MaxRealLifetime
	local homing = projectile.Homing
	setHoming(batch, item, homing ~= nil)
	batch.HomingConfig[item] = homing
	batch.HomingSource[item] = if homing then projectile.Source else nil
	batch.HomingMainSearch[item] = homing ~= nil and projectile.Filter ~= nil
	-- (remaining holds the carried debt until dispatch adds the frame's budget)
	Sweep.WriteInput(batch.Input, item, spec, filter, projectile, projectile._simulationDebt)
	Store.ClearDirty(slot)
end

-- Motion spec id for a projectile's per-shot constants (see
-- Sweep.MotionSpec), by value; new ids are sent to every worker and become
-- usable next frame. nil if not usable yet (or the values can't be keys).
local NIL = newproxy()
local values = table.create(15) -- scratch
local function lookupSpec(projectile: any): number?
	local node = specIds
	values[1], values[2], values[3] = projectile.Acceleration or 0, projectile.AccelerationDirection, projectile.Gravity or 0
	values[4], values[5], values[6], values[7] = projectile.MinSpeed, projectile.MaxSpeed, projectile.Radius, projectile.Lifetime
	local homing = projectile.Homing
	values[8] = homing and homing.TurnRate
	values[9] = homing and (homing.AcquireRadius ~= nil or homing.TargetTag ~= nil or homing.TargetTags ~= nil)
	values[10] = homing and (homing.Retarget and not homing.Permalock)
	values[11] = homing and projectile.Filter == nil
	values[12] = homing and homing.AcquireRadius
	values[13] = homing and homing.AcquireInterval
	values[14] = homing and homing.ReacquireRate
	values[15] = homing and tagMaskOf(homing)
	for index = 1, 15 do
		local value = values[index]
		if value == nil then
			value = NIL
		elseif value ~= value then
			return nil -- NaN can't be a key; the serial path deals with it
		end
		local nextNode = node[value]
		if not nextNode then
			if index == 15 then
				if nextSpecId >= MAX_SPECS then
					return nil
				end
				nextSpecId += 1
				nextNode = nextSpecId
				specReady[nextNode] = frame + 1
				local spec = Sweep.SpecOf(projectile)
				spec.TagMask = values[15]
				for _, worker in workers do
					worker.Actor:SendMessage("Motion", nextNode, spec)
				end
			else
				nextNode = {}
			end
			node[value] = nextNode
		end
		node = nextNode
	end
	return node :: any
end

-- An efficient projectile with no per-projectile overrides has exactly its
-- compiled config's motion constants, so its spec id is cached per handle
-- metatable (one per config) and packing it skips lookupSpec. (Full
-- projectiles share one metatable and carry their own `_w`: never cached.)
local specByMetatable: { [any]: number } = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" }) :: any

local function specFor(projectile: any): number?
	local plainHandle = rawget(projectile, "_slot") ~= nil and rawget(projectile, "_x") == nil
		and rawget(projectile, "_w") == nil
	local metatable = if plainHandle then getmetatable(projectile) else nil
	local id = metatable and specByMetatable[metatable]
	if not id then
		id = lookupSpec(projectile)
		if id and metatable then
			specByMetatable[metatable] = id
		end
	end
	return if id and specReady[id] <= frame then id else nil
end

-- Its scale, filter id and motion spec id if it may have a slot right now,
-- else nil.
-- Per handle metatable (one per compiled config), what packing a plain
-- efficient projectile needs beyond its Store columns: its filter id, spec id
-- and MaxRealLifetime -- filled the first time one of them is packed the
-- slow way (eligible), used by fastAcquire.
type HandleInfo = { Filter: number, Spec: number, MaxRealLifetime: number }
local handleInfo: { [any]: HandleInfo } = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" }) :: any

local function plainHandle(projectile: any): boolean
	return rawget(projectile, "_slot") ~= nil and rawget(projectile, "_x") == nil and rawget(projectile, "_w") == nil
end

local function eligible(projectile: any): (number?, number?, number?)
	if not projectile._slot then
		return nil, nil, nil -- (released: it's gone)
	end
	local scale = scaleOf(projectile)
	if not scale then
		return nil, nil, nil
	end
	local filter = filterFor(projectile)
	local spec = specFor(projectile)
	if filter and spec and plainHandle(projectile) then
		local metatable = getmetatable(projectile)
		if not handleInfo[metatable] then
			handleInfo[metatable] = { Filter = filter, Spec = spec, MaxRealLifetime = projectile.MaxRealLifetime }
		end
	end
	return scale, filter, spec
end

-- Swap-removes slot `item`.
local function release(batch: Batch, item: number)
	local last = batch.Count
	local projectiles = batch.Projectiles
	projectiles[item]._parallelState = nil
	if item ~= last then
		local input = batch.Input
		local o = (item - 1) * IN
		bufferCopy(input, o, input, (last - 1) * IN, IN)
		projectiles[item] = projectiles[last]
		batch.Slot[item] = batch.Slot[last]
		batch.Generation[item] = batch.Generation[last]
		batch.Scale[item] = batch.Scale[last]
		batch.Deadline[item] = batch.Deadline[last]
	end
	-- (the released item's flag goes, the last item's moves into its place)
	setHoming(batch, item, batch.Homing[last] == true)
	setHoming(batch, last, false)
	batch.HomingConfig[item], batch.HomingSource[item], batch.HomingMainSearch[item] =
		batch.HomingConfig[last], batch.HomingSource[last], batch.HomingMainSearch[last]
	batch.HomingConfig[last], batch.HomingSource[last], batch.HomingMainSearch[last] = nil, nil, nil
	projectiles[last] = nil
	batch.Count = last - 1
end

local function releaseBatch(batch: Batch)
	local projectiles = batch.Projectiles
	for item = 1, batch.Count do
		projectiles[item]._parallelState = nil
		projectiles[item] = nil
	end
	table.clear(batch.Homing)
	table.clear(batch.HomingConfig)
	table.clear(batch.HomingSource)
	table.clear(batch.HomingMainSearch)
	batch.Count, batch.Sent, batch.HomingCount = 0, 0, 0
end

-- Empties every slot and the queue (parallel movement paused or off).
local function releaseAll()
	for _, batch in batches do
		releaseBatch(batch)
	end
	for _, projectile in queue do
		projectile._parallelState = nil
	end
	table.clear(queue)
end

-- `fn(projectile)`: its combined time scale when it may move in parallel,
-- else nil. Called when a projectile is packed or repacked.
function Parallel.SetEligibility(fn: (any) -> number?)
	scaleOf = fn
end

-- Packs a freshly fired efficient projectile straight into a slot from the
-- values its creator already has (Projectile.Fire) -- no eligibility reads,
-- no lookups. False when it can't (parallel movement off, a batch in flight
-- -- it would also be stepped serially this frame --, its filter or spec
-- not yet known to the workers): Offer it instead.
function Parallel.PackNew(projectile: any, position: Vector3, velocity: Vector3, scale: number,
	rayParams: RaycastParams, deadline: number): boolean
	if not running or inFlight or not (scale > 0) then
		return false
	end
	local filter = filterByParams[rayParams]
	if not filter or filterReady[filter] > frame then
		return false
	end
	local spec = specByMetatable[getmetatable(projectile)]
	if not spec or specReady[spec] > frame then
		return false
	end
	local batch = batches[1]
	if not batch then
		return false
	end
	for w = 2, #workers do
		local candidate = batches[w]
		if candidate and candidate.Count < batch.Count then
			batch = candidate
		end
	end
	local item = batch.Count + 1
	if item > batch.Capacity then
		resize(batch, batch.Capacity * 2)
	end
	batch.Count = item
	local slot = rawget(projectile, "_slot")
	batch.Projectiles[item] = projectile
	batch.Slot[item] = slot
	batch.Generation[item] = Store.Generation[slot]
	batch.Scale[item] = scale
	batch.Deadline[item] = deadline
	setHoming(batch, item, false)
	-- (remaining holds the carried debt -- none yet -- until dispatch adds the budget)
	Sweep.WriteInputValues(batch.Input, item, spec, filter, position, velocity, 0, 0)
	projectile._parallelState = SLOTTED
	return true
end

-- Asks for a slot for `projectile` (call after it stepped serially or was
-- created). Packed at the next Dispatch if it's still eligible then.
function Parallel.Offer(projectile: any)
	if running and not projectile._parallelState then
		projectile._parallelState = QUEUED
		table.insert(queue, projectile)
	end
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Frame
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Packs a queued plain efficient projectile from its Store columns, with no
-- metatable reads: the same checks as eligible + pack (parallelScale's),
-- read straight from the columns, and its config's cached filter / spec.
-- False when anything is unusual (no cached info yet, its time scale or sync
-- state needs streaming...): the caller takes the ordinary path.
local function fastAcquire(projectile: any, batch: Batch, now: number): boolean
	local info = handleInfo[getmetatable(projectile)]
	if not info or filterReady[info.Filter] > frame or specReady[info.Spec] > frame then
		return false
	end
	local slot = rawget(projectile, "_slot")
	local flags = buffer.readu8(Store.Flags, slot)
	if bit32.band(flags, bit32.bor(Store.Dead, Store.Synced)) ~= 0 then
		return false
	end
	local cold = slot * Store.ColdStride
	local deadline = buffer.readf64(Store.Cold, cold + 8) + info.MaxRealLifetime
	if not (now < deadline) then
		return false
	end
	-- scale: own * source's, the ordinary case only (else parallelScale decides)
	local s = slot * S_SCALE
	local own = buffer.readf64(Store.Scales, s)
	local index = buffer.readu32(Store.Scales, s + 8)
	local sourceScale: any = if index ~= 0 then Store.Sources[index].TimeScale else 1
	if not (type(sourceScale) == "number" and sourceScale >= 0 and own >= 0 and sourceScale < LIMIT and own < LIMIT) then
		return false
	end
	local scale = sourceScale * own
	-- (a changed scale has to be streamed first: parallelScale does that)
	if not (scale > 0 and scale < LIMIT) or scale ~= buffer.readf64(Store.Cold, cold + 16) then
		return false
	end
	local m = slot * S_MOTION
	local motion = Store.Motion
	for offset = 0, 20, 4 do
		if not (abs(buffer.readf32(motion, m + offset)) <= LIMIT) then
			return false
		end
	end
	local item = batch.Count + 1
	if item > batch.Capacity then
		resize(batch, batch.Capacity * 2)
	end
	batch.Count = item
	batch.Projectiles[item] = projectile
	batch.Slot[item] = slot
	batch.Generation[item] = Store.Generation[slot]
	batch.Scale[item] = scale
	batch.Deadline[item] = deadline
	setHoming(batch, item, false)
	local t = slot * S_TIME
	local o = (item - 1) * IN
	local input = batch.Input
	buffer.writeu32(input, o, info.Spec)
	buffer.writeu32(input, o + 4, info.Filter)
	bufferCopy(input, o + IN_MOTION, motion, m, 24)
	writef64(input, o + IN_AGE, buffer.readf64(Store.Time, t))
	-- (remaining holds the carried debt until dispatch adds the frame's budget)
	writef64(input, o + IN_REMAINING, buffer.readf64(Store.Time, t + 8))
	Store.ClearDirty(slot)
	buffer.writef64(Store.Cold, cold + 24, SLOTTED) -- (_parallelState)
	return true
end

-- Packs queued projectiles and sends this frame's batches. `allowed` false
-- (e.g. debug rays on) pauses parallel movement: every slot is released and
-- everything steps serially.
function Parallel.Dispatch(activeCount: number, globalDt: number, allowed: boolean)
	local clock = os.clock
	local setupStarted = clock()
	for _, batch in batches do
		batch.Sent = 0
	end
	if refreshWorkers() then
		releaseAll() -- (batches follow worker order; this only happens at startup)
	end
	local workerCount = #workers
	running = Parallel.Enabled and allowed and workerCount > 0 and activeCount >= Parallel.MinProjectiles and globalDt > 0
	if not running then
		releaseAll()
		return
	end
	frame += 1
	syncTimeWorld()
	batchTimeVersion = ChunkManager.GetTimeVersion()
	batchUniform = ChunkManager.IsTimeUniform()
	for w = 1, workerCount do
		local batch = batches[w]
		if not batch then
			batches[w] = newBatch()
		elseif batch.Capacity > MIN_CAPACITY and batch.Count * 4 < batch.Capacity then
			-- (the whole buffer is copied to the worker each frame)
			resize(batch, math.max(MIN_CAPACITY, batch.Count * 2))
		end
	end

	-- the queue: into the emptiest batch
	local acquireStarted = clock()
	local acquired = 0
	local acquireNow = clock()
	for _, projectile in queue do
		local batch = batches[1]
		for w = 2, workerCount do
			if batches[w].Count < batch.Count then
				batch = batches[w]
			end
		end
		if plainHandle(projectile) then
			if fastAcquire(projectile, batch, acquireNow) then
				acquired += 1
				Profile.Count("FastAcquired", 1)
				continue
			end
			Profile.Count("FastMissed", 1)
		end
		projectile._parallelState = nil
		if projectile.Dead then
			continue
		end
		local scale, filter, spec = eligible(projectile)
		if not scale or not filter or not spec then
			continue
		end
		local item = batch.Count + 1
		if item > batch.Capacity then
			resize(batch, batch.Capacity * 2)
		end
		batch.Count = item
		pack(batch, item, projectile, filter, spec, scale)
		projectile._parallelState = SLOTTED
		acquired += 1
	end
	table.clear(queue)

	-- this frame's step budget for every slot: its record's remaining field
	-- holds the carried debt (written by pack and Apply), so this is a
	-- sequential pass over each batch
	local loopStarted = clock()
	for w = 1, workerCount do
		local batch = batches[w]
		local input, scales = batch.Input, batch.Scale
		for item = 1, batch.Count do
			local o = (item - 1) * IN + IN_REMAINING
			writef64(input, o, globalDt * scales[item] + readf64(input, o))
		end
	end

	local homingStarted = clock()
	-- this frame's homing state for every homing item: its target's position
	-- (fixed for the frame -- entities only move during physics; looked up
	-- once per target), its Source's index in the frame's target list, its
	-- flags and its timers (copied from Store). Target searches happen on the
	-- workers, from the frame's target list; a config with a custom Filter
	-- searches here instead, for any search due during this frame's budget.
	local HOMING_IN = Sweep.HomingInStride
	local S_HOMING = Store.HomingStride
	table.clear(goalCache)
	local anyHoming = false
	for w = 1, workerCount do
		if batches[w].HomingCount > 0 then
			anyHoming = true
			break
		end
	end
	if anyHoming then
		buildHomingFrame()
	end
	for w = 1, workerCount do
		local batch = batches[w]
		if batch.HomingCount <= 0 then
			continue
		end
		local homingIn = batch.HomingIn
		if not homingIn or buffer.len(homingIn) < batch.Capacity * HOMING_IN then
			homingIn = buffer.create(batch.Capacity * HOMING_IN)
			batch.HomingIn = homingIn
		end
		local homingFlags, projectiles, slots, input = batch.Homing, batch.Projectiles, batch.Slot, batch.Input
		local configs, sources, mainSearch = batch.HomingConfig, batch.HomingSource, batch.HomingMainSearch
		for item = 1, batch.Count do
			local h = (item - 1) * HOMING_IN
			if not homingFlags[item] then
				buffer.writeu8(homingIn, h, 0)
				continue
			end
			local projectile = projectiles[item]
			local homing = configs[item]
			local target = rawget(projectile, "HomingTarget")
			local goal = goalOf(target)
			local timers = slots[item] * S_HOMING
			local homingTimers = Store.HomingTimers
			if mainSearch[item] and homing and buffer.readf64(homingTimers, timers) <= 0 then
				local budget = readf64(input, (item - 1) * IN + IN_REMAINING) -- (already scaled)
				local searched = false
				if not goal then
					if (homing.AcquireRadius or homing.TargetTag or homing.TargetTags)
						and buffer.readf64(homingTimers, timers + 8) <= budget then
						projectile._acquireTimer = homing.AcquireInterval * (0.5 + math.random())
						searched = true
					end
				elseif not homing.Permalock and homing.Retarget and target ~= homing.Target
					and buffer.readf64(homingTimers, timers + 16) <= budget then
					projectile.ReacquireTimer = homing.ReacquireRate
					searched = true
				end
				if searched then
					local searchStarted = clock()
					target = Homing.acquireTarget(projectile, homing, projectile.Position)
					Profile.Add("HomingSearch", clock() - searchStarted)
					Profile.Count("HomingSearches", 1)
					rawset(projectile, "HomingTarget", target)
					goal = goalOf(target)
					-- (a new target can switch its continuous pose stream on or off)
					Replication.updateSyncState(projectile)
				end
			end
			local flags = Sweep.HomingFlag
			if goal then
				flags += Sweep.HomingTargetPosition
				buffer.writef32(homingIn, h + 8, goal.X)
				buffer.writef32(homingIn, h + 12, goal.Y)
				buffer.writef32(homingIn, h + 16, goal.Z)
			end
			if target ~= nil then
				flags += Sweep.HomingHasTarget
				if homing and target == homing.Target then
					flags += Sweep.HomingExplicit
				end
			end
			buffer.writeu8(homingIn, h, flags)
			buffer.writeu32(homingIn, h + 4, frameTargetIndex[sources[item]] or 0)
			bufferCopy(homingIn, h + 24, homingTimers, timers, 24)
		end
	end
	Profile.Add("HomingDispatch", clock() - homingStarted)
	local sendStarted = clock()
	local keys = entityChunkKeys()
	local slots = 0
	for w = 1, workerCount do
		local batch = batches[w]
		local count = batch.Count
		slots += count
		if count > 0 then
			batch.Sent = count
			inFlight = true
			local homes = batch.HomingCount > 0
			workers[w].Actor:SendMessage("Sweep", frame, batch.Input, count, batchUniform, keys,
				if homes then batch.HomingIn else nil, if homes then homingFrame else nil)
		end
	end
	stats.Frames += 1
	Profile.Add("DispatchSetup", acquireStarted - setupStarted)
	Profile.Add("DispatchAcquire", loopStarted - acquireStarted)
	Profile.Add("DispatchLoop", sendStarted - loopStarted)
	Profile.Add("DispatchSend", clock() - sendStarted)
	Profile.Count("Slots", slots)
	Profile.Count("Acquired", acquired)
end

-- (Pass 1 of Apply lives in ApplyPass.luau, a small module of its own so it
-- always gets native code.)

-- Applies this frame's results. `mark` is the step loop's frame mark (written
-- into the record of every projectile handled here), `now` its os.clock(),
-- `timeVersion` ChunkManager's current time version. A plain "moved, hit
-- nothing" result for an untouched projectile is written straight into its
-- record and slot; anything else goes to `apply` (see Applier). Batches a
-- worker hasn't finished (or never got) are released -- those projectiles
-- just step serially and are offered again.
function Parallel.Apply(apply: Applier, mark: number, now: number, timeVersion: number)
	local clock = os.clock
	local decodeTime, loopTime, slowTime, releaseTime, releases, kept = 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0
	local transferred = 0
	local plainTime = 0
	local slowest, total, any = 0, 0, false
	inFlight = false
	local sameVersion = timeVersion == batchTimeVersion
	for w, batch in batches do
		local count = batch.Sent
		if count == 0 then
			continue
		end
		batch.Sent = 0
		local worker = workers[w]
		local result = worker and results[worker.Id]
		local data = result and result.Data
		if not result or not data or result.Frame ~= frame or result.Count ~= count then
			stats.Late += count
			releases += batch.Count
			releaseBatch(batch)
			continue
		end
		-- (the event already handed us our own copy of the worker's buffer)
		local decodeStarted = clock()
		result.Data = nil
		local ms = result.Ms
		slowest, total, any = math.max(slowest, ms), total + ms, true
		transferred += buffer.len(data)
		local input = batch.Input
		local projectiles, slots, generations, scales, deadlines =
			batch.Projectiles, batch.Slot, batch.Generation, batch.Scale, batch.Deadline
		local generationOf = Store.Generation
		local loopStarted = clock()
		decodeTime += loopStarted - decodeStarted
		table.clear(released)
		-- Pass 1, buffers only: every plain result for an untouched projectile.
		-- The rest are deferred to pass 2, so the serial code (raycasts,
		-- Step, allocation) doesn't keep evicting this loop's working set.
		local dropped, slow, keptHere = 0, 0, 0
		local plainStarted = clock()
		if sameVersion then
			dropped, slow, keptHere = ApplyPass(Store.Motion, Store.Time, Store.Marks, Store.Flags, Store.Scales,
				data, input, count, slots, generations, scales, deadlines, generationOf, Store.Sources, now, mark,
				released, deferred, if batch.HomingCount > 0 then batch.Homing else nil, result.HomingOut,
				Store.HomingTimers)
		else
			for item = 1, count do
				deferred[item] = item
			end
			slow = count
		end
		kept += keptHere
		plainTime += clock() - plainStarted

		-- Pass 2: the serial code finishes the rest. Both `deferred` and the
		-- worker's contacts are in item order, so they're matched as we go.
		local slowStarted = clock()
		local contacts = result.Contacts
		local contactItems = contacts and contacts.Item
		local nextContact = 1
		result.Contacts = nil
		local homingOut = result.HomingOut
		result.HomingOut = nil
		local homingItems = batch.Homing
		if homingOut and batch.HomingCount > 0 then
			-- targets the workers searched for (Sweep: -1 none found, >0 an index
			-- into this frame's target list), before the serial pass resumes any
			local HOMING_OUT = Sweep.HomingOutStride
			for item = 1, count do
				if homingItems[item] and generationOf[slots[item]] == generations[item] then
					local change = readf64(homingOut, (item - 1) * HOMING_OUT + 24)
					if change ~= 0 then
						local projectile = projectiles[item]
						rawset(projectile, "HomingTarget", if change > 0 then frameTargets[change] else nil)
						Replication.updateSyncState(projectile)
						Profile.Count("HomingSearches", 1)
					end
				end
			end
		end
		for index = 1, slow do
			local item = deferred[index]
			local projectile = projectiles[item]
			local status, position, velocity, age, remaining, guard = Sweep.ReadOutputValues(data, item)
			local flags = readu8(Store.Flags, slots[item])
			local contact: WorkerContact? = nil
			if contactItems then
				while contactItems[nextContact] and contactItems[nextContact] < item do
					nextContact += 1
				end
				if contactItems[nextContact] == item then
					contact = {
						From = contacts.From[nextContact], Displacement = contacts.Displacement[nextContact],
						Instance = contacts.Instance[nextContact], Position = contacts.Position[nextContact],
						Normal = contacts.Normal[nextContact], Distance = contacts.Distance[nextContact],
					}
				end
			end
			local timers: { number }? = nil
			if homingOut and homingItems[item] then
				local h = (item - 1) * Sweep.HomingOutStride
				homingTimers[1], homingTimers[2], homingTimers[3] =
					readf64(homingOut, h), readf64(homingOut, h + 8), readf64(homingOut, h + 16)
				timers = homingTimers
			end
			local outcome = apply(projectile, status, position, velocity, age, remaining, guard,
				band(flags, Store.Dirty) ~= 0, scales[item], batchTimeVersion, batchUniform, contact, timers)
			local keep = false
			if outcome == REFRESH and not projectile.Dead then
				local repackStarted = clock()
				local scale, filter, spec = eligible(projectile)
				if scale and filter and spec then
					pack(batch, item, projectile, filter, spec, scale)
					keep = true
				end
				Profile.Add("SerialRepack", clock() - repackStarted)
			end
			if not keep then
				dropped += 1
				released[dropped] = item
			end
		end
		slowTime += clock() - slowStarted
		-- (releases must go highest item first; pass 2 added some out of order)
		if slow > 0 then
			table.sort(released, function(x, y)
				return x < y
			end)
		end
		local releaseStarted = clock()
		loopTime += releaseStarted - loopStarted
		-- backwards, so a swap never moves a slot that's still to be released
		for index = dropped, 1, -1 do
			release(batch, released[index])
		end
		releases += dropped
		releaseTime += clock() - releaseStarted
	end
	stats.Parallel += kept
	Profile.Add("ApplyDecode", decodeTime)
	Profile.Count("TransferKB", transferred / 1024)
	Profile.Add("ApplyLoop", loopTime - slowTime)
	Profile.Add("ApplySlow", slowTime)
	Profile.Add("ApplyPlain", plainTime)
	Profile.Add("ApplyRelease", releaseTime)
	Profile.Count("Released", releases)
	if any then
		stats.SlowestWorkerMs += slowest
		stats.WorkerMs += total
		stats.AppliedFrames += 1
	end
end

-- Per-frame totals from the step loop (Resumed: a worker stopped at a contact
-- and the serial code finished the frame).
function Parallel.AddCounts(parallel: number, resumed: number, serial: number, fallback: number)
	stats.Parallel += parallel
	stats.Resumed += resumed
	stats.Serial += serial
	stats.Fallback += fallback
end

-- Counters since the last call, then resets.
function Parallel.TakeStats()
	local snapshot = table.clone(stats)
	snapshot.Workers = #workers
	local frames = math.max(stats.AppliedFrames, 1)
	snapshot.SlowestWorkerMs = stats.SlowestWorkerMs / frames -- per frame, averaged
	snapshot.WorkerMs = stats.WorkerMs / frames
	stats.Parallel, stats.Resumed, stats.Serial, stats.Fallback, stats.Late, stats.Frames = 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0
	stats.WorkerChecks, stats.WorkerSkipped = 0, 0
	snapshot.WorkerReasons = table.clone(workerReasons)
	table.clear(workerReasons)
	for index = 1, 5 do
		workerReasons[index] = 0
	end
	stats.SlowestWorkerMs, stats.WorkerMs, stats.AppliedFrames = 0, 0, 0
	return snapshot
end

return Parallel
-- =============================================================================
-- END FILE: src/server/Projectile/Parallel.luau
-- =============================================================================

-- =============================================================================
-- BEGIN FILE: src/server/Projectile/init.luau
-- =============================================================================
--!native
--!strict
--!optimize 2
--[[
	Projectile (server)
	Server-authoritative, raycast-driven projectiles that live in dilated time.
	Every projectile steps in the local time of the chunk it currently occupies,
	so a bullet flying through a 0.2x slow zone crawls, its gravity floats, and
	its fuse burns slower — all for free. Because of that, a dilated Lifetime
	alone can't bound a projectile's real-world lifespan -- something frozen at
	0x (its own TimeScale, its Source's personal ratio, or its chunk) would
	never expire on its own. MaxRealLifetime is a separate, real-time
	(wall-clock) hard cap that always applies regardless of dilation -- see
	DEFAULT_MAX_REAL_LIFETIME / Projectile.SetDefaultMaxRealLifetime below.

	This module lives in ServerScriptService (never replicated to clients) --
	all hit-detection, lag-compensation, homing-acquisition, and damage-
	adjacent logic (raycast filters, penetration math, pierce/damage
	multipliers) stays server-only and unreadable by any client, on purpose.
	The purely cosmetic rendering half lives in ReplicatedStorage.Shared as
	ProjectileClient -- require that from client code, this module from
	server code. The two communicate only over VisualOffload's ProjSpawnBatch /
	ProjMove / ProjHitBatch / ProjSync / ProjTimeScale / ProjRay channels (see
	Projectile/Replication.luau for the sending side).

	Supported behaviours (mix and match): straight shots, ballistic gravity,
	acceleration/deceleration, bouncing (restitution), homing (explicit target or
	auto-acquire by tag(s), with optional Permalock), piercing with falloff, and
	cone bursts. Rendering can be offloaded to clients (Visualize = true): the
	server keeps only the logic. Visuals receive ProjSpawn with their current
	trajectory config and ProjHit on destruction. Finite-range observers also
	receive ProjRangeExit and a fresh authoritative spawn on re-entry; sparse
	corrections must never be lost permanently outside that range.
	On top of that there are three
	independent, orthogonal streaming mechanisms, each covering a different case
	the client can't safely reproduce on its own:
	 - Continuous sync while actively homing (self.HomingTarget ~= nil, checked
	   fresh every tick, never a static classification): the client only ever
	   sees a target's position through that target's own replication lag, which
	   differs per observer, so if it rotated toward that position locally, two
	   clients watching the same missile chase the same target could compute two
	   different flight paths. While a lock is held, the server streams
	   authoritative Position/Velocity through a persistent round-robin batch
	   capped at MAX_SYNC_UPDATES_PER_FRAME. At ordinary counts that is every
	   tick; at stress-test counts each cohort updates on alternating frames.
	   The cursor advances in real frame order and is never reset by dilation,
	   so changing GlobalTimeScale cannot merge staggered cohorts into one spike.
	   A rare ProjSync event tells clients when a visual crosses in or out of
	   continuous-sync mode.
	 - A one-shot correction on every bounce: reproducing a bounce client-side
	   requires matching the server's exact raycast resolution/timing AND
	   knowing which hits are really entities (piercable/filterable, server-only
	   knowledge -- the client has no replicated entity registry to check
	   against), neither of which the client can do reliably. So rather than
	   staying synced for the rest of its life, a bouncing projectile is only
	   ever corrected on the frame it actually bounces: that frame's ProjMove
	   batch carries one entry (Bounced = true) with the contact point and the
	   end-of-frame post-bounce Position/Velocity, which the client snaps to
	   and treats as its new local physics baseline. Between bounces (and
	   before the first one, and after the last one) the client is fully
	   unsynced and coasts on local physics, just like a non-homing,
	   non-bouncing shot.
	 - A one-shot ProjTimeScale message every time a projectile's personal/local
	   dilation actually CHANGES (Source.TimeScale * projectile.TimeScale --
	   see "Local time" below), not a continuous stream: the client can't
	   predict a ratio it's never been told, but once it knows the current
	   number it can fold it straight into the same local ChunkManager.ScaleDt
	   dead-reckoning every unsynced visual already does (see ProjectileClient's
	   render loop), exactly like it already does for chunk/world dilation
	   (which similarly replicates as sparse chunk-scale updates, not a
	   per-projectile stream).
	These three mechanisms are independent and compose freely: a homing
	projectile that also bounces stays continuously synced while locked (the
	bounce's position/velocity is folded into that same stream) and, if it
	loses its lock while bounces remain, drops to the bounce-only
	one-shot-correction mode instead of going fully local. A bounce correction
	is always applied unconditionally on receipt, whether or not the visual is
	currently in continuous-sync mode; likewise a ProjTimeScale update always
	applies unconditionally (a homing-synced visual just caches it for later,
	in case its lock later drops). All client-side simulation is purely
	cosmetic; the server always runs its own independent, authoritative Step,
	and any visual drift is corrected the instant ProjHit snaps the final
	position.

	Beams predict their linked centerline from timestamped motion seeds, with
	sparse safety/steering snapshots and immediate topology/clipping corrections.
	A body contact never teleports a distant
	back endpoint onto the leading endpoint's wall; each moving head owns its
	wall bounce/penetration timing. Client beam sections are tessellated after
	union and capped to 12 studs without limiting the beam's total reach.

	API:
	 Projectile.new(config) -> projectile
	 Projectile.Burst(config, count) -> { projectile }
	 Projectile.Compile(config) -> compiled   -- do the config work once...
	 Projectile.Fire(compiled, origin, direction) -> projectile  -- ...then fire it cheaply
	 Projectile.FireBurst(compiled, origin, direction, count) -> { projectile }
	 Projectile.SetDebugRays(enabled)            -- default off; see debugRays below
	 Projectile.SetDefaultMaxRealLifetime(seconds) -- default 60; see MaxRealLifetime below
	 Projectile.SetDebugSync(enabled)            -- see Projectile/Replication.luau
	 (Rendering API -- EnableClientRendering(), SetImpactHandler(fn) -- moved to
	 ProjectileClient (ReplicatedStorage.Shared.Projectile.Client); require that from client code.)

	 Query (server-only -- projectiles only ever live in the server's `active`
	 list. Every result is the LIVE projectile object, not a copy, so an
	 ability can read OR write any field on it directly -- e.g.
	 projectile.Damage = x, or the dedicated projectile:SetTimeScale(x) below --
	 and it takes effect on the very next Step, same tick):
	 Projectile.GetAll() -> { projectile }
	 Projectile.GetBySource(source) -> { projectile }       -- e.g. "my own live shots"
	 Projectile.GetInRadius(position, radius, options?) -> { projectile }
	    options: { Filter: (projectile) -> boolean }
	    -- Linear scan, not chunk-indexed like Entity/ChunkManager's spatial
	    -- queries -- fine at this game's projectile counts (MAX_ACTIVE_
	    -- PROJECTILES_PER_PLAYER in Shooter.server.luau caps it well below
	    -- where that would matter); revisit if a future ability calls this
	    -- every frame at very high projectile counts.

	 projectile:SetTimeScale(scale)   -- clamped >= 0; see TimeScale below

	 Events (Signal.luau -- see that module for the full API; :Connect(fn) ->
	 Connection with :Disconnect()). There is no config.OnHit anymore: connect
	 on the returned projectile instead, e.g.
	   local proj = Projectile.new(config)
	   proj.OnHit:Connect(function(hit) ... end)
	 projectile.OnHit    -- fires on EVERY contact worth reporting: an entity
	                         hit (piercing or final), a world bounce, a
	                         successful wall-penetration, or a final world
	                         stop. Does NOT fire for natural Lifetime/
	                         MaxRealLifetime expiry (nothing was actually hit).
	                         Listener receives one table:
	                           { CFrame: CFrame, Part: BasePart, Entity: Entity?,
	                             Hurtbox: ("Head" | "Body")? }
	                         Entity is nil for a pure world/wall contact.
	                         Hurtbox is which of the entity's two hurtboxes
	                         (see Entity.luau's "Head + Body hurtboxes"
	                         section) was struck -- nil alongside a nil
	                         Entity. Shooter.server.luau applies the target's
	                         HeadshotMultiplier when this is "Head". The
	                         module deals no damage itself anymore -- read
	                         projectile.Damage * projectile.DamageMultiplier
	                         (the latter already reflects PierceFalloff) and
	                         apply it yourself, e.g. via hit.Entity:TakeDamage
	                         or projectile.Source:DealDamage. This is what
	                         makes per-projectile custom effects possible
	                         (status effects, chain lightning, whatever) without
	                         touching this module.
	 projectile.OnDestroy -- fires exactly ONCE, whenever the projectile is
	                         actually removed (entity kill shot, world stop,
	                         bounces/penetration exhausted, or natural
	                         expiry). Listener receives
	                           { Position: Vector3, Normal: Vector3, Kind: string? }
	                         Kind is "entity" | "world" | nil (nil covers both
	                         a fizzled/expired shot and a bare Destroy() call),
	                         or whatever a caller passes to Destroy(result,
	                         kind) -- e.g. SpellRuntime's "detonate".
	                         Use this for exactly-once bookkeeping (e.g.
	                         Shooter.server.luau's activeProjectileCount
	                         decrement) -- OnHit is NOT exactly-once, since
	                         piercing/bouncing/penetrating fire it without
	                         destroying the projectile.

	 config (all optional unless noted):
	   Origin: Vector3          (required)
	   Direction: Vector3       (required unless TargetPosition given)
	   TargetPosition: Vector3  (aim at a world point instead of a direction)
	   Speed = 100
	   Acceleration = 0         (number: studs/s² along AccelerationDirection,
	              or current velocity when no direction is supplied; negative
	              decelerates. Vector3: arbitrary world-space acceleration)
	   AccelerationDirection = nil (optional direction for numeric Acceleration)
